questions.q: What kind of work did Jeremiah do?
Who was king when the word of Yahweh first came to Jeremiah?
questions.a: The word of Yahweh came to Jeremiah when Josiah was king.

questions.q: Who was king of Judah when the people of Jerusalem were exiled?
questions.a: Zedekiah was king of Judah when the people of Jerusalem were exiled.

questions.q: When did Yahweh choose Jeremiah to be a prophet?
questions.a: Yahweh chose Jeremiah before Jeremiah was born.

questions.q: Why did Jeremiah say he was not qualified?
questions.a: He said he was very young.

questions.q: What did Yahweh command Jeremiah to say?
questions.a: Yahweh commanded him to say everything that Yahweh commanded him to say.

questions.q: Why should Jeremiah not be afraid?
questions.a: He should not be afraid of the people because Yahweh was going to be with him and rescue him.

questions.q: What did Yahweh place in Jeremiah’s mouth?
questions.a: Yahweh placed his word in Jeremiah’s mouth.

questions.q: What was Jeremiah appointed to do over the nations and kingdoms?
questions.a: He was appointed to declare that Yahweh would destroy some nations and kingdoms and build up others.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do with his word?
What did Jeremiah see the second time Yahweh spoke to him?
questions.a: Jeremiah saw a boiling pot tipping toward him from the north.

questions.q: What was the meaning of the pot that Jeremiah saw?
questions.a: The pot was a picture of coming disaster.

questions.q: What will the clans of the kingdoms of the north do when Yahweh calls them?
questions.a: They will come and set up their thrones at the gates of Jerusalem, and their armies will attack the walls of Jerusalem and all the cities of Judah.

questions.q: Why will Yahweh pronounce sentence against Jerusalem and Judah?
questions.a: He will pronounce sentence against them because they abandoned him, burned incense to other gods, and worshiped idols that they made with their own hands.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Jeremiah to do before speaking to the people?
questions.a: Yahweh told him to get ready and say everything that Yahweh commanded him.

questions.q: What did Yahweh make Jeremiah like, to stand against the whole land?
questions.a: Yahweh made him like a fortified city, an iron pillar, and bronze walls.

questions.q: What will the people do after Jeremiah speaks to them?
questions.a: The people will fight against Jeremiah, but they will not defeat him because Yahweh will be with him to protect him.

commentary.text: Jeremiah's call to the prophetic office. (Jer. 1:1-10) A vision of an almond-tree and of a seething-pot, Divine protection is promised. (Jer. 1:11-19)

Jer. 1:1-10 Jeremiah's early call to the work and office of a prophet is stated. He was to be a prophet, not to the Jews only, but to the neighbouring nations. He is still a prophet to the whole world, and it would be well if they would attend to these warnings. The Lord who formed us, knows for what particular services and purposes he intended us. But unless he sanctify us by his new-creating Spirit, we shall neither be fit for his holy service on earth, nor his holy happiness in heaven. It becomes us to have low thoughts of ourselves. Those who are young, should consider that they are so, and not venture beyond their powers. But though a sense of our own weakness and insufficiency should make us go humbly about our work, it should not make us draw back when God calls us. Those who have messages to deliver from God, must not fear the face of man. The Lord, by a sign, gave Jeremiah such a gift as was necessary. God's message should be delivered in his own words. Whatever wordly wise men or politicians may think, the safety of kingdoms is decided according to the purpose and word of God.

Jer. 1:11-19 God gave Jeremiah a view of the destruction of Judah and Jerusalem by the Chaldeans. The almond-tree, which is more forward in the spring than any other, represented the speedy approach of judgments. God also showed whence the intended ruin should arise. Jeremiah saw a seething-pot boiling, representing Jerusalem and Judah in great commotion. The mouth or face of the furnace or hearth, was toward the north; from whence the fire and fuel were to come. The northern powers shall unite. The cause of these judgments was the sin of Judah. The whole counsel of God must be declared. The fear of God is the best remedy against the fear of man. Better to have all men our enemies than God our enemy; those who are sure they have God with them, need not, ought not to fear, whoever is against them. Let us pray that we may be willing to give up personal interests, and that nothing may move us from our duty.
